best ultra wide lens for landscape
profile_notes: Landscape glass — wide, sharp corner-to-corner, distortion-controlled. GATE: focal_length_mm <= 35 (landscape is a wide-angle discipline; specs.py stores focal as a first-number so a 16-35 -> 16 and a 24-70 -> 24 both pass correctly as landscape-usable, while a 70-200 -> 70 fails correctly). Aperture is DELIBERATELY NOT gated: landscape is shot stopped down (f/8-f/11) and the best landscape zooms are f/4 — a fast-aperture gate would wrongly exclude them. CRUX at 3: optical_performance — corner-to-corner sharpness at landscape apertures is the defining wide-lens criterion (a portrait lens can be soft in the corners; a landscape lens cannot). SECONDARY at 2: distortion (straight horizons, buildings, coastlines — barrel distortion is the classic wide-lens failure) and vignetting (even skies and gradient tones; heavy corner falloff shows on open sky). SUPPORTING at 1: chromatic_aberration (purple/green fringing on high-contrast edges — branches against sky), filter_thread (landscape shooters live on polarizers and ND filters; a usable front thread matters, and bulbous ultra-wides that can't take screw-in filters are a real limitation), build (weather sealing for the field). Deliberately UNWEIGHTED: bokeh (irrelevant stopped down), coma (that is the ASTRO lens criterion, not landscape), af_performance (manual-focus / hyperfocal work), color_rendition, handling. gear_class excludes novelty only. DISTINCT-FINGERPRINT CHECK: shares optical_performance 3 with street lenses but gates wide (focal<=35 vs <=50) and leads its secondaries with distortion+vignetting (the wide-angle failure modes) rather than handling; distinct from astro lenses (coma 3, aperture-gated) by not gating speed and not weighting coma. Ratified by Lee 2026-09-15.
